title: Isolation Request Signal Refinement and Intake Runway for Private/VPC Deploys
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: As Private/VPC/on-prem requests grow, support and eng teams spend excessive time interpreting inconsistent customer signals (e.g., 'air-gapped', 'limited egress', 'bastion only'). This increases lead time and causes incorrect intake lanes. Goal: Build a signal refinement layer + intake runway that normalizes network/upgrade constraints, surface a deterministic acceptance canvas, and auto-suggests engagement lanes (self-serve, concierge, blocked).
background: We already have ad-hoc triage notes and per-customer playbooks, but too many tickets require manual clarifications. Recent support analytics show 28% of private-deploy requests stall >3 business days waiting for network details. Existing artifacts: network-readiness-runbook, staged-onboarding-playbook; this ticket is meant to centralize signal parsing and lane assignment into an intake runway.
acceptance_criteria: A structured intake form is defined with explicit boolean fields for: egress_allowed, bastion_access, maintainers_with_admin, corporate_proxy, allowed_ports, scheduled_maintenance_windows, and patching_policy
An automated signal-refinement spec that maps 90%+ of real incoming requests to one of three lanes: self-serve, guided-concierge, blocked-requires-architecture
A lightweight scoring rubric (0-100) implemented as a decision table and documented in Confluence
Pilot intake runway integrated with Support ticket ingestion that reduces clarifying questions by >=50% during pilot customers
Clear handoff checklist for Eng/SE for requests that escalate from guided-concierge -> architecture review
decision_log: We will prioritize network signal normalization (egress/bastion/ports) before adding deeper infra compatibility checks (OS images/k8s versions)
Initial lane taxonomy will be limited to three outcomes to keep operational overhead low: self-serve, concierge, blocked
Scoring threshold for self-serve will be conservative (>=85) for pilot, then relax based on observed false positives
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers may misrepresent constraints to get faster onboarding. Mitigation: require signed readiness attestation for self-serve and random post-onboard audits
Risk: Overly strict scoring blocks viable customers. Mitigation: include a fast-appeal path and CS/SE manual override with audit trail
Risk: Engineering capacity for concierge lane could spike. Mitigation: Add capacity gating and require SE cost approval for high-touch engagements
timeline: 03/01 - 03/05: Discovery + stakeholder interviews; 03/06 - 03/18: Intake schema + rubric draft; 03/19 - 03/28: Engineering prototype + support integration; 03/29 - 04/01: Pilot with 5 customers and iterate
notes: Prototype will reuse parts of existing network-probe library. We will avoid adding new agents or proxy tech for the pilot — focus on signal clarification only. If pilot shows >30% 'blocked' due to missing customer action, we will add templated remediation guides for common blockers.

Deliver Confluence spec and decision table (by 2026-03-12)
Spin up prototype webhook that annotates incoming Support tickets with preliminary lane suggestion (by 2026-03-18)
Schedule pilot kickoff with 3 designated accounts and measure clarifying questions metric (by 2026-03-29)
Prepare escalation SOP and SE capacity gating for concierge lane (by 2026-03-22)
comments: Alina G (2026-03-02): We should include a question about existing bastion automation (e.g., Okta SSH certs) — makes handoffs faster
Ravi P (2026-03-03): Engineering prefers a small JSON schema compatible with existing probes rather than a freeform form
Nora S (2026-03-04): Support can triage 'egress_allowed' automatically if the customer attaches a network diagram in the ticket
audit_trail: Intake runway decisions will be logged to the ticketing system; any manual override requires a short rationale and approver signature
implementation_notes: Start with a standalone lambda that parses Support ticket fields and tags lane suggestion; later fold into Console intake flow. Keep telemetry minimal: counts of suggestions, final lane, clarifying questions count.
final_comment: This initiative should reduce agent time-to-first-action and create a predictable funnel for private deployments. We'll re-evaluate lane taxonomy after pilot and plan follow-up epics for enforcement and automation.
